sections.title: Philistines and Israelites prepare for battle
David hears Goliath's challenge and responds
Saul arms David and David prepares
David strikes Goliath with a stone
David beheads Goliath and takes his armor

brief.place: Valley of Elah, Judah, near Socoh and Azekah
brief.dress: Bronze Age military attire: bronze helmets, coats of mail (5000 shekels), bronze shin armor, bronze javelins; Israelite shepherd attire: simple tunic, shepherd's bag, sling, staff; no sword for David initially
brief.buildings_and_objects: weaver's beam-sized spear staff, spear head (600 shekels iron), sword sheath, shepherd's pouch with five smooth stones from brook, wagons, tents (David's armor stored in tent), camp fortifications
depiction_rules: Yahweh (God of Israel) must not be depicted as a human figure; represent divine presence through light, wind, or hand from heaven if needed
Goliath's immense size (six cubits and a span ~9.5 feet) must be visually emphasized against David's youth
David's victory is through divine aid, not weaponry—show sling and stone, not swordplay as primary
Philistines retreat in disarray after Goliath's fall; Israelites pursue to Gai, Ekron, Shaaraim, Gath
David brings Goliath's head to Jerusalem but keeps armor in his tent at battlefield
